author: GamingBolt
description:
“Why do we fall?” asked a legendary actor in one of the most acclaimed superhero films of all time. Cairn, The Game Bakers' latest title after Furi and Haven, elicited a different question during the many times that I fell. Why do I climb?

It's a sentiment that resonates all the more considering the situation that Aava, the protagonist, is in. She has no shortage of friends or people cheering her on; no lack of interests to keep her occupied. Yet, she climbs Mount Kami, which no human has ever conquered and lived to tell the tale. Why?

Probably because it's there, and that only scratches the surface of why Cairn is so endearing.
title: Cairn Review - Yet Another Spectacular PS5 Console Exclusive

author: GamingBolt
description:
Every player can remember their first time experiencing a brand-new concept in a video game. Whether it’s stepping into the first 3D space or stepping out into your first open-world adventure, those mind-blowing moments stick with us. 

We all seek to experience those moments again, but not at the expense of a bad game. Disappointment also sticks with us for a long time, and that’s what we’re here to talk about today. This video breaks down 15 revolutionary gaming concepts that got us monumentally hyped only to bore us to tears or frustrate us to no end upon release. 

Games like Starfield, Anthem, Evolve, and Marvel’s Avengers prove that innovation alone isn’t enough; great ideas still need smart design, meaningful content, and player-first decisions to succeed.
title: 15 Revolutionary Gaming Concepts That Sounded Great But Flopped Hard

author: GamingBolt
description:
Feudal Japan stories, especially in video games, often tend to fall into some familiar periods, the Bakumatsu being particularly popular. However, before the fall of the Tokugawa Shogunate, leading to the Meiji Restoration, was the era leading up to its formation, where samurai and ninja roamed the battlefields, as legendary figures clashed. That's right – the late Sengoku era, which forms a fitting backdrop for Team Ninja's Nioh series.

Now, the house that Ninja Gaiden (and Dead or Alive) is no stranger to dark fantasy. But its hack-and-slash efforts have been of the fast-paced variety. Before Nioh, it never really tussled with Souls-like mechanics, and anyway, how would that even work? How would the combo-heavy gameplay mesh with a stamina meter and switchable stances for each weapon? As it turns out, quite well.
title: NIOH 1 - The Full Story Explained - Before You Play Nioh 3
